recommendations.headline: Call quality drives outcomes far more than price: satisfied customers close at 72% vs only 15% for neutral and 8% for dissatisfied calls, yet 702 of 1,584 calls (44%) end neutral and 949 (60%) never even reach a price discussion.
behaviour: Callback is the dominant outcome (744 of 1,584 calls, 47%), far ahead of actual orders (320, 20%) or clear interest (230, 14%), showing most leads are parked rather than closed.
Price-shopping and quote-comparison dominate behaviour tags: price_shopper 218, comparing_quotes 146, indicating many callers are benchmarking rather than ready to buy.
Repeat buyers (126) and urgent buyers (123) are sizeable segments but loyalty tagging is tiny (loyal_to_us 14, referral 13), suggesting repeat business isn't being converted into advocacy.

Dealers make up over half of all calls (811 of 1,584) and convert best among high-volume segments (39% win), while 'unknown' segment calls (519, 33% of total) convert worst (26%), pointing to poor segment capture at call start.

Stock availability (211 calls) and price (208 calls) are the two most common objections, but stock_availability wins only 25% of calls versus quality_doubt-related calls winning 31%, showing availability issues hurt conversion more than quality concerns.
satisfaction: Win rate is almost entirely explained by satisfaction: satisfied calls close at 72% vs 15% neutral and 8% dissatisfied — closing the satisfaction gap is the single biggest lever available.
Only 471 of 1,584 calls (30%) are rated satisfied; 702 (44%) are neutral, meaning the majority of calls leave customers undecided rather than delighted.

Price is rarely even discussed: 949 of 1,584 calls (60%) show 'not_discussed' price reaction, while only 141 (9%) accept price outright and 39 (2%) call it too high — price objection is less about the number and more about how/when it's presented.
price_high is cited in 208 calls yet these calls still convert at 28%, similar to the overall order rate, showing price alone rarely kills a deal if the rest of the call goes well.

conversion.title: Fix slow/unclear answers first
conversion.evidence: slow_or_unclear_answer is the top rep-missed behaviour (214 instances) and neutral/dissatisfied calls convert at only 15%/8% vs 72% for satisfied.
conversion.action: Train reps to give a direct rate/stock answer within the first minute of the call before any negotiation; use a quick-reference rate sheet updated daily.

conversion.title: Always lock a follow-up date
conversion.evidence: no_follow_up_fixed happened in 201 calls, and 744 of 1,584 calls (47%) ended as 'callback' with no order.
conversion.action: Mandate every rep state and log a specific callback date/time before ending calls classified as callback; manager to audit weekly follow-up adherence.

conversion.title: Send quotes immediately, not later
conversion.evidence: no_quote_sent flagged in 128 calls; multiple non-converted summaries show customers waiting on WhatsApp quotes that never arrived.
conversion.action: Make instant WhatsApp/email quotation (with specs, no prices on calls) mandatory before call ends for any price_enquiry (530 calls) or product_info call.

conversion.title: Always ask for the order
conversion.evidence: didnt_ask_for_order occurred in 107 calls despite interested outcome count of 230.
conversion.action: Add an explicit closing script line ('Shall I book this for you today?') as a mandatory step for every call tagged interested or negotiating.

conversion.title: Offer alternatives when stock is out
conversion.evidence: stock_availability is the #1 objection (211 calls, only 25% win) and didnt_offer_alternative occurred in 71 calls.
conversion.action: Train reps to always propose an in-stock substitute brand/size/colour on the same call when the requested item is unavailable.

conversion.title: Tighten segment capture
conversion.evidence: 'unknown' segment accounts for 519 calls (33%) and converts worst at 26%, well below dealer (39%) and end_user (42%).
conversion.action: Require reps to ask and log customer type (dealer/fabricator/contractor/end-user) in the first 30 seconds of every call.

conversion.title: Protect high-win objection types
conversion.evidence: credit_terms (31% win) and quality_doubt (31% win) already convert above average; low performers are transport_cost (22%) and min_quantity (13%).
conversion.action: Build ready answers/scripts specifically for transport-cost and minimum-quantity objections, as these currently drag down overall conversion.

offers.title: Fast-track quote service
offers.for_whom: price_enquiry callers (530 calls) and comparing_quotes customers (146)
offers.why: no_quote_sent flagged 128 times; customers repeatedly ask 'can you send quotation' and 'can you send tomorrow morning'.

offers.title: Stock-alert / pre-booking for out-of-stock colours
offers.for_whom: customers needing specific colours (off-white, sky blue, Royal Blue, grey) frequently unavailable
offers.why: stock_availability is the top objection (211 calls) and multiple summaries show customers switching or dropping orders due to unavailable colour.

offers.title: Cutting/processing service packages
offers.for_whom: fabricators and contractors needing custom sizes
offers.why: cutting_processing need logged 58 times; summaries mention custom polycarbonate cutting, wastage questions, bend/profile change requests.

offers.title: Scheduled site-delivery slots
offers.why: fast_delivery is the top need (241 mentions) and delivery_time is the 3rd biggest objection (129 calls, 27% win).

offers.title: Sample/spec pack before order
offers.why: samples requested 40 times and technical_advice is the 2nd highest need (228 mentions).

offers.title: Consider evaluating a short credit-period option for established dealers
offers.for_whom: repeat/bulk dealers flagged needs_credit (45) or raising credit_terms objection (49 calls, 31% win)
offers.why: credit_terms objection already converts well (31%) suggesting flexible terms could unlock more bulk orders.

loyalty.title: Consider a tiered repeat-buyer recognition programme
loyalty.how: Track repeat_buyer tag (126 instances) and reward with priority dispatch slots or first access to new stock/colours, not discounts.
loyalty.why: repeat_buyer is a sizeable behaviour segment but loyal_to_us tagging is only 14, showing repeat purchase isn't being converted into recognised loyalty.

loyalty.title: Dedicated account manager for top dealers
loyalty.how: Assign a single point of contact for dealers (811 calls, 39% win) to reduce rep-switch confusion and speed quotes.
loyalty.why: Dealers are the largest and best-converting segment; consistent contact can reduce no_follow_up_fixed (201 instances) specifically for this group.

loyalty.title: Referral recognition scheme
loyalty.how: Formally acknowledge and thank customers who refer others (publicly or via small gesture, non-monetary) and track referral tag.
loyalty.why: referral behaviour already appears 13 times organically, showing latent word-of-mouth potential that isn't being cultivated.

loyalty.title: Regular proactive rate/stock update calls
loyalty.how: Schedule periodic update calls to regular/bulk buyers even without an active enquiry.
loyalty.why: regular_updates is a top-5 need (105 mentions) and customers explicitly ask things like 'why does rate keep changing for a regular customer like me?'

loyalty.title: Small customer-care gestures (notepads etc.) formalised
loyalty.how: Continue/extend small complimentary items (e.g., notepads) as a recognised loyalty touch for long-standing accounts.
loyalty.why: One well-converting call specifically shows a loyal customer requesting more free notepads despite buying elsewhere — a low-cost loyalty signal already working.

non_price_benefits.title: Speed and clarity of response
non_price_benefits.why: slow_or_unclear_answer is the single biggest rep-missed issue (214 calls) and directly correlates with lower satisfaction and win rates.

non_price_benefits.title: Technical expertise on specs/grades
non_price_benefits.why: technical_advice is the 2nd highest customer need (228 mentions) and needs_technical_help is the 2nd most common behaviour (196).

non_price_benefits.title: Reliable stock and consistent supply
non_price_benefits.why: stock_availability (224 need mentions, 211 objections) and consistent_supply (67 mentions) are major pain points customers want solved.

non_price_benefits.title: Fast, reliable delivery commitments
non_price_benefits.why: fast_delivery is the top customer need (241 mentions) and delivery_time is the 3rd largest objection (129 calls).

non_price_benefits.title: Quality assurance and certification
non_price_benefits.why: quality_assurance (69 mentions) and test_certificate (12 mentions) needs show customers value proof of quality, and quality_doubt objections convert at a relatively strong 31% when addressed.

non_price_benefits.title: After-sales support and issue resolution
non_price_benefits.why: after_sales_support need (24 mentions) and complaint intent (97 calls) around damaged/delayed shipments show customers value a company that fixes problems promptly.

top_questions.question: What is the current rate for [product]?
top_questions.answer_tip: Confirm the product/spec first, give today's rate promptly without hesitation, and flag if a rate change is expected so the customer can decide quickly.

top_questions.question: Is [colour/size] in stock right now?
top_questions.answer_tip: Check live stock before answering; if unavailable, immediately offer the closest in-stock alternative colour/size instead of ending the call.

top_questions.question: Can you send the quotation today/now?
top_questions.answer_tip: Commit to a specific time (same call if possible) and actually send it via WhatsApp/email before the call ends.

top_questions.question: Can you reduce the price / match a competitor's rate?
top_questions.answer_tip: Avoid discussing rupee cuts; instead highlight consistent supply, quality assurance, and service reliability as reasons for the current rate.

top_questions.question: Will delivery happen by [specific day/time]?
top_questions.answer_tip: Give a realistic committed delivery window and proactively update the customer if there's any delay, rather than waiting for them to follow up.

top_questions.question: Can this be done on credit / month-end payment?
top_questions.answer_tip: Explain current payment terms clearly; if flexibility is possible, escalate to a manager rather than an outright refusal on the call.

top_questions.question: Why did the price increase suddenly?
top_questions.answer_tip: Explain market-driven rate changes transparently and suggest locking in the current rate quickly if they're ready to order.

top_questions.question: Why hasn't my payment/delivery/issue been resolved?
top_questions.answer_tip: Acknowledge the issue, give a specific resolution timeline, and follow up proactively rather than asking the customer to call back.
